body:
N-27 SLICE 2 DESIGN, part 2 of 2 (B-131).

WHERE (server, slice 2a, one PR): a small module server/encore_server/encore_server/ref_janitor.py run as one more errand of the hourly library link (errands() in api.py, after the finders). At most 500 refs a pass, ONE SQL statement with NOT EXISTS for each pointer table of part 1 (the playback_state queue by a LIKE on the id inside the JSON text, deliberately over-cautious: a false 'pointed at' only keeps a row longer), the file_log rows of the retired refs deleted in the same transaction, one log line with the count, and NEVER a migration (it removes rows, it adds no column). TESTS FIRST: a ref pointed at by each table in turn survives; an unpointed one older than 14 days goes; a fresh one stays; a live verdict keeps it, an expired one does not; a merged survivor stays; the 500 limit; the queue JSON case; a second pass finds nothing.

THE PHONE SIDE (slice 2b, separate app PR): a library row (is_ref=1) with no file, like, playlist entry, download or play of the person, absent from every feed page and older than 14 days is dropped by the same pass that already drops unused rows. dropUnused only sees the ids a feed page carries, which is why the row a tap leaves behind lives for ever: give it its own age rule, do not widen the feed. A row the person is looking at (an open playlist page, the queue) is never dropped.

NOT DOING: retiring anything the person liked or listed; a timer in the app without the server's view; a cron outside the server's own errands. REMOVAL TRIGGER: none, it is the permanent hygiene of the table; the SOURCE of junk (browsing makes rows) was removed in slice 1 (branch task/N-27-browsing-makes-no-rows), so this only clears what exists and what real taps leave behind.

FIRST STEP FOR A HELPER: the failing tests above, then the janitor. Docs: docs/18 (data) one paragraph, AUDIT B-131 and B-126 closed with the PR numbers, a CHANGELOG line, the state-table row if one names the junk.
